lines.trans: We have exactly ten minutes before the cake cools down and rejects any warm glaze!
Grab your purse, Nour! The corner shop next to the clock tower sells local honey!
I am running! Keep the cake warm, Salma, and tell Mazen to wait patiently!
Run like the wind, Nour! A perfect historic recipe depends entirely on your speedy feet!
Good afternoon, Rami! I need a jar of your best golden honey, faster than lightning!
Whoa, Nour! Are you chasing a thief, or did someone accidentally eat a raw hot pepper?
Neither! We are baking the thirty-year-old mystery cake and the honey jar is empty!
Oh, a culinary emergency! Here is a fresh jar of spring blossom honey, on the house.
You are a lifesaver, Rami! We will save you a slice if Mazen does not eat it all!
Wait—do not just brush it on plain! Read the botanical book first!
What book? Salma is melting it in a pot the second I sprint through the courtyard gate!
Trust me! Tell Suad to smell the paper where the recipe card rested!

meanings.note: The word 'معنا' (معنا) means 'معنا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معنا عشر دقايق بالزبط قبل ما تبرد الكيكة وترفض أي طبقة تلميع دافية!
examples.trans: We have exactly ten minutes before the cake cools down and rejects any warm glaze!
This is معنا.

meanings.note: The word 'دقايق' (دقايق) means 'دقايق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معنا عشر دقايق بالزبط قبل ما تبرد الكيكة وترفض أي طبقة تلميع دافية!
examples.trans: We have exactly ten minutes before the cake cools down and rejects any warm glaze!
This is دقايق.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: The word 'تبرد' (تبرد) means 'تبرد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معنا عشر دقايق بالزبط قبل ما تبرد الكيكة وترفض أي طبقة تلميع دافية!
examples.trans: We have exactly ten minutes before the cake cools down and rejects any warm glaze!
This is تبرد.

meanings.note: The word 'الكيكة' (الكيكة) means 'الكيكة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خليني أشوف من نظاراتي: ادهني الكيكة الدافية بمعلقتين من... تلطيخة زرقا!
examples.trans: Let me look through my glasses: Brush warm cake with two spoons of... blue smudge!
This is الكيكة.

meanings.note: The word 'وترفض' (وترفض) means 'وترفض'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معنا عشر دقايق بالزبط قبل ما تبرد الكيكة وترفض أي طبقة تلميع دافية!
examples.trans: We have exactly ten minutes before the cake cools down and rejects any warm glaze!
This is وترفض.

meanings.note: In questions أي means 'which?' (أي علبة؟ 'which tin?'); in conditionals/negatives it means 'any' (أي شي 'anything').

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Used for a coat of paint (طبقة دهان), a layer of pastry, or a building storey.

examples.text: الطبقة الأولى نشفت وصارت جاهزة للطبقة التانية.
examples.trans: The first coat has dried and is ready for the second coat.

examples.text: دهان المي بيكفيه طبقتين رقيقتين عشان يطلع ناعم.
examples.trans: Water-based paint only needs two thin coats to come out smooth.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: The word 'دافية' (دافية) means 'دافية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنتاج بسيط! صينية رقم واحد رح تاخد طبقة سكر وفانيليا دافية؛ هادا تشطيب كلاسيكي.
examples.trans: Simple deduction! Tin One gets a warm vanilla sugar glaze; that is a classic finish.
This is دافية.

meanings.note: The word 'خدي' (خدي) means 'خدي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خدي جزدانك يا نور! الدكانة اللي عالزاوية جنب برج الساعة بتبيع عسل بلدي!
examples.trans: Grab your purse, Nour! The corner shop next to the clock tower sells local honey!
This is خدي.

examples.trans: Grab your purse, Nour! The corner shop next to the clock tower sells local honey!
This is جزدانك.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: The word 'الدكانة' (الدكانة) means 'الدكانة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خدي جزدانك يا نور! الدكانة اللي عالزاوية جنب برج الساعة بتبيع عسل بلدي!
examples.trans: Grab your purse, Nour! The corner shop next to the clock tower sells local honey!
This is الدكانة.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: The word 'عالزاوية' (عالزاوية) means 'عالزاوية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'next to, beside'.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أبراج.

examples.trans: The downtown clock tower is old.
We heard the tower bell at noon.

meanings.note: The word 'الساعة' (الساعة) means 'الساعة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: راقبي الساعة يا نور—بعد أربعين دقيقة من هلق، لازم هدول الكيكات الصغيرة التلاتة يكونوا مثاليين.
examples.trans: Watch the clock, Nour—forty minutes from now, these three mini cakes must be perfect.
This is الساعة.

meanings.note: The word 'بتبيع' (بتبيع) means 'بتبيع'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: From بلد ('country, town'); prized on Jordanian market stalls for local olive oil, honey, lemons, and thyme.

examples.text: عسل بلدي من جبال عجلون ريحته بتشهي.
examples.trans: Local honey from the Ajloun hills smells delicious.
We bought yellow local lemons for tea.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

examples.trans: Let us carry it straight to Salma in Room Nine before anyone breathes too hard!

examples.trans: This book actually belonged to Rami and his aunt before it reached the lending shelf!
This is لـ.

examples.trans: I pressed the bell once upstairs, Mazen, and your friendly wire rang twice as usual.
This is مازن.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

examples.trans: Run like the wind, Nour! A perfect historic recipe depends entirely on your speedy feet!
This is كليا.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: The word 'رجليكي' (رجليكي) means 'رجليكي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اركضي متل الريح يا نور! الوصفة التاريخية المثالية بتعتمد كليا على رجليكي السريعين!
examples.trans: Run like the wind, Nour! A perfect historic recipe depends entirely on your speedy feet!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: The word 'رامي' (رامي) means 'رامي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هادا الكتاب كان أصلا لـ رامي وعمته قبل ما يوصل لرف الإعارة!
examples.trans: This book actually belonged to Rami and his aunt before it reached the lending shelf!
This is رامي.

meanings.note: The word 'بدي' (بدي) means 'بدي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: مسا الخير يا رامي! بدي مرطبان من أحسن عسل ذهبي عندك، أسرع من البرق!
examples.trans: Good afternoon, Rami! I need a jar of your best golden honey, faster than lightning!
This is بدي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a glass jam, honey, or olive jar (dual مرطبانين, plural مرطبانات).

examples.trans: We lined the jars of jam and honey up on the shelf.
Open the new jar of honey for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of منيح ('good'). Before a noun without ال- it means 'the best' (أحسن نومة 'the best sleep').

examples.trans: This is the best room in the house.
I feel better today.

meanings.note: The word 'ذهبي' (ذهبي) means 'ذهبي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اطوي التوت الكامل شوي شوي بخليط اللوز واخبزيه أربعين دقيقة ليصير لونه ذهبي.
examples.trans: Fold whole berries gently into the almond batter and bake forty minutes until golden.
This is ذهبي.

meanings.note: The word 'عندك' (عندك) means 'عندك'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: مسا الخير يا رامي! بدي مرطبان من أحسن عسل ذهبي عندك، أسرع من البرق!
examples.trans: Good afternoon, Rami! I need a jar of your best golden honey, faster than lightning!

examples.text: مسا الخير يا رامي! بدي مرطبان من أحسن عسل ذهبي عندك، أسرع من البرق!
examples.trans: Good afternoon, Rami! I need a jar of your best golden honey, faster than lightning!

examples.text: مسا الخير يا رامي! بدي مرطبان من أحسن عسل ذهبي عندك، أسرع من البرق!
examples.trans: Good afternoon, Rami! I need a jar of your best golden honey, faster than lightning!
This is البرق.

meanings.note: The word 'ول' (ول) means 'ول'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ول يا نور! عم تلحقي حرامي، ولا حدا أكل فليفلة حارة نية بالغلط؟
examples.trans: Whoa, Nour! Are you chasing a thief, or did someone accidentally eat a raw hot pepper?
This is ول.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: The word 'تلحقي' (تلحقي) means 'تلحقي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ول يا نور! عم تلحقي حرامي، ولا حدا أكل فليفلة حارة نية بالغلط؟
examples.trans: Whoa, Nour! Are you chasing a thief, or did someone accidentally eat a raw hot pepper?
This is تلحقي.

meanings.note: The word 'حرامي' (حرامي) means 'حرامي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ول يا نور! عم تلحقي حرامي، ولا حدا أكل فليفلة حارة نية بالغلط؟
examples.trans: Whoa, Nour! Are you chasing a thief, or did someone accidentally eat a raw hot pepper?
This is حرامي.

meanings.note: With two pronunciations in context: walla ('or' in choice questions: عالشارع ولا عالساحة؟) and wala ('not even / nor': ولا خدش 'not a single scratch', ولا يهمك 'do not worry at all').

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'someone / anyone'; with ما في (ما في حدا) it means 'nobody'.

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باكل, بياكل).

examples.trans: The brothers are eating lemon cake in the courtyard.
We ate a hot breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: The word 'فليفلة' (فليفلة) means 'فليفلة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ول يا نور! عم تلحقي حرامي، ولا حدا أكل فليفلة حارة نية بالغلط؟
examples.trans: Whoa, Nour! Are you chasing a thief, or did someone accidentally eat a raw hot pepper?
This is فليفلة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حارات.

examples.trans: The shop is right here in our neighbourhood.
Old Amman neighbourhoods are peaceful.

meanings.note: The word 'نية' (نية) means 'نية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ول يا نور! عم تلحقي حرامي، ولا حدا أكل فليفلة حارة نية بالغلط؟
examples.trans: Whoa, Nour! Are you chasing a thief, or did someone accidentally eat a raw hot pepper?
This is نية.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: The word 'منهم' (منهم) means 'منهم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ولا واحد منهم! عم نخبز الكيكة الغامضة تبعت التلاتين سنة ومرطبان العسل فاضي!
examples.trans: Neither! We are baking the thirty-year-old mystery cake and the honey jar is empty!
This is منهم.

examples.text: ولا واحد منهم! عم نخبز الكيكة الغامضة تبعت التلاتين سنة ومرطبان العسل فاضي!

examples.text: ولا واحد منهم! عم نخبز الكيكة الغامضة تبعت التلاتين سنة ومرطبان العسل فاضي!
examples.trans: Neither! We are baking the thirty-year-old mystery cake and the honey jar is empty!
This is الغامضة.

meanings.note: The word 'التلاتين' (التلاتين) means 'التلاتين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ولا واحد منهم! عم نخبز الكيكة الغامضة تبعت التلاتين سنة ومرطبان العسل فاضي!
examples.trans: Neither! We are baking the thirty-year-old mystery cake and the honey jar is empty!
This is التلاتين.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: The word 'العسل' (العسل) means 'العسل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بالزبط يا زياد. وصينية رقم تلاتة رح تاخد الورقة الرابحة تبعتي: دهنة خفيفة من العسل الدافي.
examples.trans: Exactly, Ziad. And Tin Three gets my wild card: a thin brush of warm honey.
This is العسل.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فاضية, plural: فاضيين).

examples.trans: Is room six vacant tonight?
The street outside the gate is completely empty.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: The word 'حالة' (حالة) means 'حالة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أوه، حالة طوارئ بالمطبخ! تفضلي هادا مرطبان طازج من عسل زهور الربيع، على حساب المحل.
examples.trans: Oh, a culinary emergency! Here is a fresh jar of spring blossom honey, on the house.
This is حالة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طوارئ.

examples.trans: We have a small emergency in the kitchen!
The emergency key hangs beside the door.

meanings.note: The word 'بالمطبخ' (بالمطبخ) means 'بالمطبخ'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أوه، حالة طوارئ بالمطبخ! تفضلي هادا مرطبان طازج من عسل زهور الربيع، على حساب المحل.
examples.trans: Oh, a culinary emergency! Here is a fresh jar of spring blossom honey, on the house.
This is بالمطبخ.

examples.text: تفضلوا، هادا كتاب أعشاب الحديقة المغلف بقماش من رف مكتبة الكتب المستعملة بـ شارع الياسمين!
examples.trans: Here is the cloth-bound garden herb book from the second-hand bookshop shelf on Jasmine Street!
This is هادا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طازجة, plural: طازجين).

examples.trans: Morning bread is fresh and hot!
Fresh orange juice and fresh cake.

examples.trans: Oh, a culinary emergency! Here is a fresh jar of spring blossom honey, on the house.

meanings.note: The word 'الربيع' (الربيع) means 'الربيع'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Oh, a culinary emergency! Here is a fresh jar of spring blossom honey, on the house.
This is الربيع.

meanings.note: Also used in the warm hospitality phrase على حسابنا ('on our tab / on the house').

examples.trans: The bill is thirty-eight dinars.
The first coffee today is on the house!

meanings.note: The word 'المحل' (المحل) means 'المحل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أوه، حالة طوارئ بالمطبخ! تفضلي هادا مرطبان طازج من عسل زهور الربيع، على حساب المحل.
examples.trans: Oh, a culinary emergency! Here is a fresh jar of spring blossom honey, on the house.
This is المحل.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one man.

examples.trans: Did you plant these herbs yourself?
Did you plan this entire meeting?

meanings.note: The word 'منقذ' (منقذ) means 'منقذ'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إنت منقذ يا رامي! رح نخليلك شقفة إذا مازن ما أكلها كلها!
examples.trans: You are a lifesaver, Rami! We will save you a slice if Mazen does not eat it all!
This is منقذ.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: The word 'نخليلك' (نخليلك) means 'نخليلك'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إنت منقذ يا رامي! رح نخليلك شقفة إذا مازن ما أكلها كلها!
examples.trans: You are a lifesaver, Rami! We will save you a slice if Mazen does not eat it all!
This is نخليلك.

examples.trans: You are a lifesaver, Rami! We will save you a slice if Mazen does not eat it all!

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

examples.trans: You are a lifesaver, Rami! We will save you a slice if Mazen does not eat it all!
This is أكلها.

examples.text: إنت منقذ يا رامي! رح نخليلك شقفة إذا مازن ما أكلها كلها!
examples.trans: You are a lifesaver, Rami! We will save you a slice if Mazen does not eat it all!
This is كلها.

meanings.note: The word 'استني—لا' (استني—لا) means 'استني—لا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استني—لا تدهنيها لحالها سادة! اقرأي كتاب النباتات بالأول!
examples.trans: Wait—do not just brush it on plain! Read the botanical book first!
This is استني—لا.

meanings.note: The word 'تدهنيها' (تدهنيها) means 'تدهنيها'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Wait—do not just brush it on plain! Read the botanical book first!
This is لحالها.

meanings.en: plain; solid-coloured; without pattern or sugar
meanings.note: Invariable adjective used after nouns for plain paper, fabric, or unsweetened coffee (قهوة سادة).

examples.text: جبت ورق سادة عشان الرسم يبين.
examples.trans: I brought plain paper so the drawing shows clearly.

examples.text: بدي فنجان قهوة سادة لو سمحت.
examples.trans: I'd like a cup of plain black coffee, please.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: The word 'النباتات' (النباتات) means 'النباتات'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Wait—do not just brush it on plain! Read the botanical book first!

examples.trans: What book? Salma is melting it in a pot the second I sprint through the courtyard gate!
This is تذوبها.

meanings.note: The word 'بطنجرة' (بطنجرة) means 'بطنجرة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أي كتاب؟ سلمى رح تذوبها بطنجرة أول ما أركض من بوابة الساحة!
examples.trans: What book? Salma is melting it in a pot the second I sprint through the courtyard gate!
This is بطنجرة.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: The word 'أركض' (أركض) means 'أركض'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: What book? Salma is melting it in a pot the second I sprint through the courtyard gate!
This is أركض.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: The word 'وثقي' (وثقي) means 'وثقي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Trust me! Tell Suad to smell the paper where the recipe card rested!

examples.trans: Blue smudge is not an ingredient sold at the Saturday market, Suad!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian noun for any retail shop or spot (pl. محلات).

examples.trans: Below is the signature of the antique shop.
There's a pastry shop next to the house.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The word 'اللقاء' (اللقاء) means 'اللقاء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
This is اللقاء.

meanings.note: Polite imperative for females.

examples.trans: Here is the go ahead (f).
I like the go ahead (f).

meanings.note: Definite form of courtyard.

examples.trans: Here is the the courtyard.
I like the the courtyard.

meanings.note: Passive participle for placed or put.

examples.trans: Here is the placed.
I like the placed.

meanings.note: Imperative verb for a female to read.

examples.trans: Here is the read.
I like the read.

meanings.note: Definite form of goodness, used in greetings.

examples.trans: Here is the the goodness.
I like the the goodness.

meanings.note: Adverb meaning by mistake.

examples.trans: Here is the by mistake.
I like the by mistake.

meanings.note: Definite form of recipe.

examples.trans: Here is the the recipe.
I like the the recipe.

meanings.note: Definite form of a piece of paper.

examples.trans: Here is the the single paper.
I like the the single paper.

meanings.note: Feminine possessive particle.

examples.trans: Here is the belonging to (f).
I like the belonging to (f).

meanings.note: Number ten.

examples.trans: Here is the ten.
I like the ten.
